question_text: Distinguish fibre-optic cabling from wireless transmission in terms of reliability in a factory with metal partitions and electrical interference.
adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
solution: Wireless signals can be weakened/blocked by metal partitions.; This can cause packet loss/retransmission or variable connectivity.; Fibre carries light within a cable and resists electromagnetic interference.; It therefore gives more predictable links here, although a cut/bent fibre can still fail.
